title: Basic Contrast Mechanisms in Electron-Beam Induced Current (EBIC) Images of High Impedance Samples
content: EBIC imaging in the scanning electron microscope (SEM) is a well-established characterization technique for the study of electronic materials, including solar cells [1]; however, its application in the scanning transmission electron microscope (STEM) is less common. The hardware implementation of EBIC imaging in electron microscopes is not well-described in the literature and the cost of EBIC systems is elevated, limiting accessibility for many research institutions. This work outlines simple ways to add EBIC imaging in conventional SEMs and STEMs. We also describe the basic contrast mechanisms of the technique, proposing (to the best of our knowledge) a novel effect observed in the dielectric regions of biasing sample carriers. These descriptions would allow researchers to expand the use of EBIC imaging beyond the well-known contrast mechanism at play in systems with built-in potential barriers (also referred to as the “standard EBIC” mechanism).
